Definition: properly, to sigh, i.e. breathe strongly; by implication, to be sorry, i.e. (in a favorable sense) to pity, console or (reflexively) rue; or (unfavorably) to avenge (oneself)
BiblicalUsage: Nacham means to be sorry, to repent, to sigh deeply, and it is used for God relenting and for people turning. In Genesis 6:6 it repented the Lord that He had made man, and it grieved Him at His heart, and in Exodus 32:14 the Lord repented of the evil He thought to do to His people after Moses prayed. In 1 Samuel 15:11 it repenteth the Lord that He set up Saul as king, and in Joel 2:13 the people are told to rend their hearts and turn to the Lord, for He is gracious and repenteth Him of the evil.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe repentance is the hinge of the whole Bible, because God relents when His people turn, and He grieves when they will not. The Lord's repenting is not Him changing His mind like a man, but His mercy answering a prayer and a turned heart. I hold that Joel's call still stands: rend your heart, not your garments, and turn.
